summary: Gyokusen Hosaka (1887–1964) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as president (学長) of Komazawa Junior College from circa 1950 to 1962 and taught Stanley Weinstein.
Gyomay Kubose (1905–2000) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu between circa 1937 and 1941.
Gyoon Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015). He held a post as vice director (副主任) at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).

Gyoshu Chojo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Chojo served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).

Gyula Benigny (1890–1966) worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a Ph.D. at Eötvös Loránd University (~1908–1912). He taught at Debrecen Reformed Theological University and served as docent and extraordinary professor at the University of Debrecen.
Gyula Ortutay (1910–1978) studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934). He held a post at Nyugat and taught András Róna-Tas.
Gyula Wojtilla (born 1945) is an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1964–1969) under János Harmatta (~1963–1968) and at Banaras Hindu University (~1973–1974).

Gyurme Dorje (1950–2020) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from the University of Edinburgh and SOAS, held fellowships at the University of London, and served as a translator at the Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

György Hazai (1932–2016) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1949–1954) and held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung (~1963–1982).

György Kara (1935–2022) was a linguistics and Central Asian studies scholar educated at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University. He held professorships at Eötvös Loránd University and Indiana University Bloomington.

Gyōin Hashimoto (1897–1978) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Join Saeki. He served as head of Yakushiji (1939–1967) and head of Hōssō-shū (1940).

Gábor Kovács is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Dharma Gate Buddhist College and Corvinus University of Budapest. In 2018, he became an Associate Professor at Corvinus University of Budapest.
Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Gérard Barrigue de Fontainieu (1863–1927) was an Indology scholar who earned a diploma from INALCO by 1891. He served as a pensionnaire at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1901 to 1902.

Gérard Colas (born 1952) is an Indologist. He has served as a Directeur de recherche and Senior Fellow at the CNRS/National Centre for Scientific Research and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Gérard Cotton was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Joseph Mansion and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Liège by 1930.

Gérard Devèze was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Julien Vinson. He earned a diploma in Tamil from INALCO by 1885 and also obtained a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) specialized in Indology, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, he headed a unit at the CNRS (~1984–2003) and served as Professor at the Collège de France (1984–2011), succeeding Jean Filliozat.
